properties.areaDesc: Coastal waters from Baffin Bay to Port Aransas out 20 NM; Waters from Baffin Bay to Port Aransas from 20 to 60 NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 27 at 12:56AM CDT until October 27 at 1:30AM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
SMWCRP

The National Weather Service in Corpus Christi has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Baffin Bay to Port Aransas out 20 NM...
Waters from Baffin Bay to Port Aransas from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 130 AM CDT.

* At 1256 AM CDT, a shower capable of producing waterspouts was
located 31 NM southeast of Malaquite Beach, or 41 NM southeast of
Port Aransas, moving northwest at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can create locally hazardous seas.

* Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters from Baffin Bay to Port Aransas out 20 NM and
Waters from Baffin Bay to Port Aransas from 20 to 60 NM.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.areaDesc: Alamosa, CO; Conejos, CO; Costilla, CO; Rio Grande, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 11:55PM MDT until October 27 at 11:45AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Conejos County in south central Colorado...
West Central Costilla County in south central Colorado...
Southeastern Rio Grande County in south central Colorado...
Southwestern Alamosa County in southeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 1145 AM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Widespread
inundation of agriculture fields, wetlands, and other low-lying
areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1155 PM MDT, Gauge reports continue to indicate high stream
flows. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Alamosa, San Luis Valley Airport, Sanford, La Jara and Alamosa
East.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Palm Beach County
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 27 at 1:22AM EDT until October 28 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8
to 13 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
moderate coastal flooding. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Wednesday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Wednesday evening. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 AM EDT early this morning.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 8 PM EDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Guam Coastal Waters; Rota Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued October 27 at 3:09PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Typhoon In-fa is expected to pass through the far northern CNMI
somewhere between just north of Saipan to as far north as Maug
island sometime on Friday. Winds and seas will increase late
Thursday ahead of the approaching typhoon, potentially exceeding
hazardous levels to small craft by Friday morning, with seas
peaking at 8 to 12 feet. Mariners are urged to take precautions
and remain weather aware over the coming days.

properties.areaDesc: Tinian Coastal Waters; Saipan Coastal Waters

properties.description:
Typhoon In-fa is expected to pass through the far northern CNMI
somewhere between just north of Saipan to as far north as Maug
island sometime on Friday. Winds and seas will sharply increase
late Thursday ahead of the approaching typhoon, quickly exceeding
hazardous levels to small craft by early Friday morning, with seas
peaking at 12 to 16 feet. Seas up to 20 feet remain possible if
In-fa takes a southern track. Mariners are urged to take
precautions and remain weather aware over the coming days.

properties.areaDesc: Montezuma, CO; San Juan, UT
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 11:07PM MDT until October 27 at 8:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Catastrophic flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected along the San Juan River between Four Corners and Mexican
Hat. This is an emergency situation!

* WHERE...Western Montezuma County in southwestern Colorado...
Southern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along San Juan River is occurring or expected to
begin shortly. The crest has occurred at Bluff and will work toward
Mexican Hat through sunrise.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1106 PM MDT, - At 10:30 PM MDT Monday the stage was 23.9 feet
at Bluff
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:30 PM MDT Monday was 26.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue to fall at Bluff and
fall below flood stage early Tuesday morning.
- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 32.0
feet on 09/10/1927.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mexican Hat, Tselakai Dezza, Bluff, Halchita, Montezuma Creek and
Aneth.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 26 at 8:59PM PDT until October 30 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 2.1 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Pablo Bay, San
Francisco Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. More substantial impacts are expected along bayshore
Marin County where increased flooding is anticipated across
low lying areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 2.1 ft above normal (7.9 ft MLLW) at 12:15 PM
Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at 12:56 PM
Wednesday 10/28, 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 01:43 PM
Thursday 10/29, and 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 02:39
PM Friday 10/30. These predictions include up to 1.2 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.
